label: fed-back u in the later copy phase
explanation: Token-specific feature. It fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the model own fed-back input is u (essentially 100% of mass has in_tok u). It is silent on u in the original phase, on <DEL>, and on every other token. It needs the copy to be past its first couple of outputs: there are no activations at recall_idx 0-1, they are rare at recall_idx 2, and the rate plateaus around 3.4% from recall_idx 4 on, conditional only on the input. It is suppressed when many outputs remain (to_go >= 6 never fires, to_go 5 is rare). The strongest activations, up to ~3.3, are short sequences where u was the 3rd original token and is fed back near the end of the copy (e.g. l p u z <DEL> l p [u]). Remaining false positives are mostly u fed back early in long sequences, which are inactive. A refinement, u & (recall_idx>=3 | to_go<=1) & to_go<=4, reaches dev F1 0.948.

issues: The factual claims check out on the dev profile. All activation mass is in the copy phase: original and <DEL> steps have 0 actives. in_tok 'u' accounts for 54830 of 54949 actives and 1.000 of the mass; other tokens give about 120 scattered actives, the most being 57 on 's'. recall_idx 0 and 1 have 0 actives, recall_idx 2 has 2902 (rate 0.006), and from recall_idx 4 on the rate is 0.033-0.034. to_go >= 6 has 0 actives and to_go 5 has 898. The max is 3.269, on 'l p u z <DEL> l p [u]', and the top examples are short sequences (L=3-6) with u fed back near the end of the copy.

There is a systematic residual, which the explanation already acknowledges. The real condition is relative position (u fed back late in the copy, i.e. small to_go), and recall_idx>=3 only stands in for it. Test misses (2901 steps, 3.5% of mass) are all at recall_idx 2 in short sequences (L=3/4), e.g. 'f u z <DEL> f [u:0.73]'. False positives (6387 steps) are mostly u at recall_idx 3-4 in long sequences (L=6-9) with many outputs still to go, e.g. 'q c u m v q c c j <DEL> q c *u* m v q c c', inactive.

Test scores for alternatives: bare 'u in copy phase' F1 0.745 (precision 0.594). 'recall_idx >= to_go' (u fed back in the second half of the copy) F1 0.938. The agent's refinement u & (recall_idx>=3 | to_go<=1) & to_go<=4 has test F1 0.947, precision 0.914, recall 0.981, mass recall 0.997, compared with 0.917 for the kept predicate.
The label 'fed-back u in the later copy phase' fits the refined, relative-position reading and does not overclaim. The kept predicate is a slightly worse version of it, not a different explanation.
